newsitem.title: INDONESIA: East Timor youths get light sentences.
newsitem.headline: East Timor youths get light sentences.

text.p: Five East Timorese youths have been sentenced to six and a half months in jail, minus time spent in custody, on charges relating to disturbances last December, Indonesia's official Antara news agency reported on Monday.

The youths were part of a group of 16 arrested after violent incidents in a crowd of tens of thousands of people who had gathered in the East Timor capital Dili to welcome local Nobel Peace prize laureate Bishop Carlos Belo.
One soldier in civilian clothes was killed after he was reportedly found carrying a pistol and a hand-held radio in the grounds of the city's cathedral.

The report did not say how much time the youths had spent in custody and whether they were released after the sentencing, which was lighter than the 12 months the prosecution asked for. It also did not specify the exact nature of their crimes.

Judge Agustinsu Rungu said during the sentencing in Dili's state court at the weekend that he had awarded a light sentence as none of the youths had criminal records, they were all young and had acted politely during the trial.
The report said five more youths remain to be tried but did not give details on the fate of the six other defendants.

East Timor was invaded by Indonesia in December 1975 and annexed the following year in an act not recognised by the United Nations, which regards Portugal as being the administering power in its former colony abandoned by Lisbon in 1974.
